notes: The DO-ORP coupling, but pushed past the qualitative statement the slice already carries and onto the question of whether either channel can be believed. ORP verification is A6.5: orp-zobells-shelf-life-01 (90 days chilled at 4 C), orp-table653-25c-430-01 and orp-table653-values-01 (theoretical ZoBell Eh by temperature, 430 mV at 25 C, 443 at 20, 418 at 30), orp-example-22c-01 (the worked check passes within plus/minus 5 mV of the table value), orp-field-cal-equilibrate-01 and orp-equilibrate-15-30-01 (15-30 minutes to thermal equilibrium in the ZoBell), orp-interpolate-tables-01, orp-quinhydrone-30c-01. A6.8 supplies the troubleshooting hook that makes the temperature dependence the first thing to suspect when the check fails (mp-t6-zobell-temperature-11) and the routing of a bad ORP reading back to A6.5 (mp-t6-parameter-chapter-map-06). The DO half of turn 2 is A6.0: a60-xcut-tbl601-all-01 (plus/minus 0.2 mg/L for optical DO) and a60-xcut-sw-60s-median3-01 / a60-xcut-gw-median5-01 (median of the final three or five readings). ORP has no criterion in that table, so A6.5's own constant-potential cadence (orp-reading-cadence-01, orp-thermal-equilibrium-30min-01) is what governs it — a distinction no single file states. Predicted rag: the slice has the DO/ORP coupling and 'trend beats absolute value', but no ZoBell values, no temperature table, and no stabilisation numbers.

turns.content: ORP at one of our pods has slid about 120 mV over two weeks while oxygen has barely moved — still sitting near 6. Before I go tell anyone there's something organic going in upstream, how do I prove the ORP probe itself isn't the thing that's drifting?

must_contain: tells the operator to check the probe against ZoBell's solution rather than judging drift from the trace alone
states the expected ZoBell value is temperature dependent and must be read from the temperature table, not taken as a single number
gives the theoretical ZoBell Eh at 25 C as about 430 mV
states values for temperatures between table rows are interpolated
states the solution and sensors must be left to reach thermal equilibrium, on the order of 15 to 30 minutes, before the check is read
gives the pass window for the check as agreement within roughly 5 mV of the table value
warns that the ZoBell solution has a limited shelf life (about 90 days kept chilled near 4 C), so an old bottle can fail the check on its own
must_not: gives a single ZoBell millivolt value with no temperature attached
invents a ZoBell value or tolerance not in the manual
answers only that ORP falls as oxygen is consumed and never gives a probe check
recommends quinhydrone without noting it is not recommended and is unstable above 30 C

turns.content: And the oxygen side — it moves about 0.3 mg/L between readings at that site. Is that noise or is that a real change I should be logging?

must_contain: gives the USGS stabilisation criterion for optical dissolved oxygen as about plus or minus 0.2 mg/L across five or more consecutive readings
concludes a spread of about 0.3 mg/L exceeds that criterion, so the sensor has not stabilised and the reading is not yet reportable
tells the operator to allow longer equilibration and take further readings, then report the median of the final readings
gives the median rule as the final three or more readings in surface water, or the final five or more in groundwater
notes that ORP is not covered by that stabilisation table and is instead judged by the potential holding constant over the reading sequence
must_not: invents a dissolved-oxygen stabilisation threshold other than the manual's
treats a 0.3 mg/L spread as within criteria
reports a mean instead of the median
applies the dissolved-oxygen criterion to the ORP channel
